metadata.description: Hand-authored 1930-era strategic resource locations for the Para Bellum map. Coal/lignite basins, iron-ore districts, oil fields (polygons) and major iron & steel works (points). Covers the western Sprint-2 region (Benelux + Western Germany, features 1-12, authored Sprint 3) AND the Sprint-6 eastward expansion — eastern Germany, Poland, Czechoslovakia and Austria (features 13-48, authored Pre-Sprint 9.0).
metadata.source: Authored from public-domain period industrial geography (Ruhr, Saar, Sambre-Meuse/Borinage, Campine/Limburg, Liège, Lorraine; Upper Silesia, Dąbrowa, Lower Silesia, Ostrava-Karviná, North Bohemia, Sokolov, Central German and Lusatian lignite, Styrian lignite; Siegerland, Lahn-Dill, Peine-Salzgitter, Erzberg, Częstochowa, Nučice; Galician and Vienna-Basin oil). No licensed boundary or concession data was used. Public-domain compatible per AD-018.
metadata.review_status: REVIEWED-EAST (Pre-Sprint 9.0) — western features 1-12 remain the Sprint-3 DRAFT, unchanged and still pending Matthew's historical review. Eastern features 13-48 were authored against the significance rule below and cross-checked feature-by-feature against data/boundaries/boundaries_1930.geojson (zero attribution disagreements). Coordinates are approximate basin/district/works centroids.
notes: OIL IS NOW PRESENT. The Sprint-3 file recorded 'oil has no 1930 in-bbox source (none authored)'. That is superseded: Galician oil (Borysław-Tustanowice-Drohobycz, Bitków-Nadwórna, Krosno-Jasło) is inside the east bbox and was Polish in 1930, and is now authored. Ploiești (~44.9°N) remains BELOW the bbox min_lat 46.3 and is deliberately not reachable.

SIGNIFICANCE RULE used for the eastern pass: include a field/works if its ~1930 output was materially significant at national scale (order 5 Mt/yr or more for coal), OR if it was a nation's only or principal source of that resource. The second clause is what admits Austrian Styrian lignite, Czechoslovak Nučice ore and Gbely oil, and the German Hannover oil points — small absolute producers that are nonetheless the whole of that nation's domestic supply.

OWNERSHIP: the `country` property is DOCUMENTATION ONLY. The owning nation of a tagged hex is decided by data/boundaries/boundaries_1930.geojson (point-in-polygon in the sampler), never by this property.

The Upper Silesian Coal Basin is authored as ONE feature spanning the 1922 partition because it is one geological and industrial district; its `country` is 'POL/DEU'. The partition line is irregular (Beuthen/Gleiwitz/Hindenburg German, Chorzów/Katowice/Rybnik Polish) and is NOT reproduced here — the boundaries file resolves each hex. Dąbrowa is a separate feature because it was a separate basin under the Russian partition, Polish since 1918.

EXCLUDED — Zistersdorf (Lower Austria) oil. First crude was raised in August 1930 at sub-commercial rates; the first profitable well (Gösting II) was drilled in 1934. At a 1 January 1930 scenario start it is anachronistic, so it is not authored. This is a deliberate exclusion, not an oversight.

CAVEAT — Peine-Salzgitter iron. The Peine (Ilsede) ore was worked continuously for the Ilseder Hütte and is correct for 1930. The large-scale Salzgitter development is 1937+ (Reichswerke 'Hermann Göring'); the field is authored at its 1930 working extent, not its wartime extent.

CAVEAT — German domestic iron ore was minor in 1930 (roughly a quarter of supply; Sweden and France covered the rest). Siegerland, Lahn-Dill and Peine are authored because they were genuinely producing, but a boolean resource model cannot express that Germany's ore was low-grade and insufficient. Treat German iron as present-but-thin when tuning yields.
Polygons are coarse basin/district outlines, not licensed boundary data. Points are single works or single small fields (one point tags exactly one hex).

Polygons tag a hex only when the HEX CENTRE falls inside. At 10 km hexes a district smaller than roughly 0.2° lon x 0.15° lat may tag nothing — small single-site fields are therefore authored as points.
resource_type in {coal, steel, iron, oil}. `agriculture` is NOT authored here; it is derived from OSM landuse in the sampler.

Saar coalfield and most of the Lorraine (Briey/Thionville) iron basin lie at or just south of the Sprint-2 bbox min_lat (49.4); those features are included for completeness but only hexes inside a given bbox are tagged.

Features 13-48 also fall inside the wceurope and (Siegerland/Lahn-Dill only) Benelux bboxes. Those artifacts are STALE with respect to this file until regenerated; only the east artifact was regenerated in Pre-Sprint 9.0.

properties.name: Upper Silesian Coal Basin (Katowice-Beuthen-Rybnik)
properties.note: One geological/industrial district spanning the 1922 partition; boundaries_1930.geojson resolves per-hex ownership. Europe's second basin after the Ruhr.

properties.name: Dąbrowa Coal Basin (Sosnowiec-Dąbrowa Górnicza)
properties.note: Ex-Russian-partition basin, Polish since 1918; geologically continuous with Upper Silesia, kept separate for documentation.

properties.name: Köflach-Voitsberg Lignite (Styria)
properties.note: Austria's principal coal district; small in absolute terms, admitted under the only/principal-source clause.

properties.name: Lahn-Dill Iron Ore District (Dillenburg-Wetzlar)
properties.note: Added Pre-Sprint 9.0, not on the candidate list: with Siegerland one of the two German ore districts actually producing in 1930.

properties.name: Peine-Salzgitter Iron Ore Field
properties.note: Peine/Ilsede ore worked for the Ilseder Hütte in 1930; the large-scale Salzgitter development is 1937+ (Reichswerke). Authored at 1930 working extent.

properties.name: Częstochowa Iron Ore Basin
properties.note: Poland's principal domestic ore source; low-grade sideritic ore feeding Huta Częstochowa.

properties.name: Nučice / Prague Basin Iron Ore (Barrandian)
properties.note: Added Pre-Sprint 9.0, not on the candidate list: Czechoslovakia's only domestic ore district of note; the ore-to-works pair for Kladno.

properties.name: Donnersmarckhütte (Hindenburg O.S. / Zabrze)
properties.note: Added Pre-Sprint 9.0: works Germany retained in its share of Upper Silesia after the 1922 partition.

properties.name: Poldi Works (Kladno)
properties.note: The Kladno coal district itself is deliberately NOT authored (below the significance rule); the works are.

properties.name: Borysław-Tustanowice-Drohobycz Oil Field (Galicia)
properties.note: The dominant European oil field inside this bbox; Polish in 1930. Ploiești is below min_lat and unreachable by design.

properties.name: Krosno-Jasło Oil Field (Western Galicia)
properties.note: The oldest Galician field (Bóbrka); much declined by 1930 but still producing.

properties.name: Gbely (Egbell) Oil Field
properties.note: Industrial extraction from 1914; Czechoslovakia's only domestic oil. Authored as a point (one hex) to reflect its marginal scale.

properties.name: Wietze Oil Field (Hannover)
properties.note: Added Pre-Sprint 9.0: Germany's oldest oil field, still producing in 1930 at a scale far below national need. Authored as a point so German oil reads as token, not absent.
